```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(geoscales)
```

## The GeoScale object

A `GeoScale` is an S7 object, a subclass of `nestedscales`' `NestedScale`.
`S7::prop_names()` lists its properties, `gs@geoframes` or
`S7::prop(gs, "geoframes")` reads one, and `str(gs)` prints them with their
size and purpose (with `nestedscales` 0.3.0 or later).

```{r}
gs <- geoscale_example()
S7::prop_names(gs)
```

| property | type | holds |
|---|---|---|
| `@leaftable` | `data.frame` | one row per **leaf**: one column per geoframe, and the weight columns |
| `@geoframes` | `character` | the hierarchy, ordered coarsest first (the same value as `@frames`) |
| `@members` | named `list` | the ordered code vocabulary at each geoframe |
| `@leaf` | `character` | the name of the column that identifies the leaves: the finest geoframe, unless another was named |
| `@labels` | `data.frame` | display names by `(geoframe, region, variant)`; sparse |
| `@geometry` | `sfc` or `NULL` | optional leaf polygons, aligned to leaftable rows |
| `@meta` | `list` | `name`, `desc`, `weights`, `default_weight`, `default_label`, `crs`, `source` |
| `@attributes`, `@aliases` | `data.frame` | inherited from `NestedScale`: member values and alternative spellings |

The object is a **definition**: the regions, the geoframes that group them
and the weights that size them. It holds no data. Data stays in ordinary
tables, tied to the object by the region-code columns. Everything else — parent/child
tables, ancestry, shares, dissolved shapes — is derived on demand; nothing
is cached on the object.

## The leaftable

```{r}
geoscale_leaftable(gs)
```

Each row is one leaf. The finest geoframe (`cell` here) is the **authored
node ID** (unique, non-missing) and the leaf column, `geoscale_leaf_column(gs)`; there
is no separate identifier column. Coarser geoframe columns may hold `NA` — a leaf
with no
code at a coarser geoframe (a rest-of-world row, offshore areas) simply
does not participate at that resolution, and `na_action=` decides what
recasts do about it.

## Geoframes, members, ranks

```{r}
geoscale_geoframes(gs)
geoscale_geoframes(gs, finest = TRUE)   # the leaf geoframe
geoscale_regions(gs, "state")           # the members at one geoframe
geoscale_rank(gs, c("zone", "cell"))    # positions, coarsest = 1
```

Geoframe names must be syntactically valid column names;
`CORE_GEOFRAMES` is recommended vocabulary, not enforcement:

```{r}
CORE_GEOFRAMES
is_valid_geoframe(c("COUNTRY", "reg32", "", "2bad"))
```

Navigation is derived on demand from the leaftable — and because
geoframes may cross-cut, ancestry is computed leaf-mediated, never as a
transitive closure:

```{r}
geoscale_parents(gs, "zone", "ZB", target = "state")   # cross-cut: two parents
geoscale_ancestors(gs, "cell", "A5")
geoscale_descendants(gs, "country", "N")
head(geoscale_ancestry(gs), 4)
```

## Weights and meta

```{r}
geoscale_weights(gs)
gs@meta[c("name", "weights", "default_weight")]
```

`meta$name` is load-bearing: conversion and attach name their working
columns after the object (`geoscale_map()` label columns,
`join_geoscale()`'s `"<name>."` prefixes), so both require a named
GeoScale. `geoscale_build()` derives a default name from the geoframes;
`geoscale_from_leaftable()` takes `name=`.

## Labels

Display names are declared per geoframe and per region, in named variants.
The table is sparse: here the countries get a name and an alternative one,
while states and zones have none and are shown by their codes.

```{r}
gs_named <- gs |>
  attach_labels_geoscale(
    data.frame(geoframe = "country", region = c("N", "S"),
               label = c("Northland", "Southland")),
    variant = "name"
  ) |>
  attach_labels_geoscale(
    data.frame(geoframe = "country", region = "N", label = "Nordland"),
    variant = "de"
  )
geoscale_labels(gs_named)
geoscale_label(gs_named, c("N", "S"), "country")
geoscale_label(gs_named, c("N", "S"), "country", variant = "de")
geoscale_label(gs_named, c("N1", "ZB"), "zone")
```

Subsets keep the labels of the regions that remain, and the plots use the
default variant.

## What the validator guarantees

Construction (any layer: `geoscale_from_provider()`,
`geoscale_build()`, `geoscale_from_leaftable()`) enforces:

- the leaf column present, character, unique, no missing/empty values;
- every label row naming a geoframe and a region that exist;
- every geoframe present as a leaftable column; members exactly the
  non-`NA` values of that column, in a stable order;
- weights numeric, finite, non-negative, with a positive sum;
  `default_weight` one of the declared weights;
- geometry, when attached, aligned 1:1 with leaftable rows (see
  `attach_geometry_geoscale()`; the CRS is recorded in `meta$crs`);
- a warning (not an error) when geoframes look ordered finer-to-coarser
  — order carries meaning: aggregation direction follows it.

## The registries

Three package-level registries change behavior explicitly — the only
way anything global changes:

**Rules** map value-column names to their aggregation rule (there is no
fallback — unregistered columns without `rule=` error):

```{r}
GEOSCALE_RULES
register_geoscale_rule("capacity", "sum")
register_geoscale_rule("eff", "weighted_mean", weight = "pop")
get_geoscale_rule("eff")
list_geoscale_rules()
clear_geoscale_rules()
```

**Maps** hold exact crosswalks that short-circuit the leaf-layer
derivation in `geoscale_map()` — for hand-audited concordances:

```{r}
fake <- data.frame(state = "N1", zone = "ZC", n_from = 1L,
                   n_overlap = 1L, w = 1, w_from = 1)
register_geoscale_map(gs, "state", "zone", fake)
list_geoscale_maps()
get_geoscale_map(gs, "state", "zone")
clear_geoscale_maps()
```

**Providers** are named map sources (`fetch` functions returning a wide
`sf`/`data.frame`); the package ships one:

```{r}
list_geoscale_providers()
get_geoscale_provider("naturalearth")$desc
```
